correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, the adjacent XOR map bijects nonconstant binary n-windows modulo complement with nonzero binary (n-1)-windows. The sum of the bits of every punctured cycle is 2^(n-2), even, so it integrates in exactly two globally complementary cyclic words. The missing zero self-loop at state 0^(n-2) is inserted or deleted uniquely in an Euler circuit. In the complete de Bruijn graph on N=2^(n-2) states, A^(n-2)=J implies nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues 2, so the directed tree count is 2^(N-1)/N, and BEST yields exactly that many cycles. Distinct windows give full period and exclude a rotation-complement stabilizer. The exhaustive direct n=3..5 test and independent exact reduced-Laplacian computations at difference orders 2..6 passed; no finite result is substituted for the all-order proof.

A de Bruijn order-(n-1) cycle contains every binary (n-1)-window, including the all-zero one, whereas a bipartition universal cycle has only nonzero adjacent-XOR windows. The correspondence requires deleting the unique all-zero loop and verifying integrability.

originality.rationale: The closest 2015 complete paper proves existence and liftability of binary two-block partition universal cycles but does not state the exact enumeration or the adjacent-XOR/zero-loop bijection with de Bruijn cycles. The de Bruijn count and the corresponding integer sequence are classical, and the claim is restricted to the new identification and all-order enumeration of the partition-encoding class. Semantic record searches and an actual read of the highly relevant paper found no equivalent statement. Residual historical priority risk remains, including the inaccessible full text of an early foundational paper.

value.rationale: A universal cycle is a compact exhaustive schedule for a natural family of two-block partitions. The exact count for all n quantifies design diversity at double-exponential scale (log2 U_n=2^(n-2)-n+1), while the constructive, reversible difference/loop map permits use of existing de Bruijn-generation and sampling methods. This is a natural all-order invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice, known numerical table repackaging, or a claim of a new construction.
